newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga upgrades Snorre oil reserves 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Saga upgrades Snorre oil reserves 16 pct.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Thursday it had upgraded recoverable reserve estimates at the North Sea Snorre field by 16 percent to 1.315 billion barrels of oil.
Saga said the new figure was 71 percent higher than the original estimate of 767 million barrels, which was the basis for the decision to develop the field in 1988.
"The degree of recovery has increased from 25 percent in the plan for development and operation to 37 percent today," a statement from the company said.
It attributed the upgrade to new technology, improved geological understanding of the reservoir and new, advanced production methods.
Further plans for the development of the Snorre area will be presented in 1997, Saga said.

Saga, as operator of Snorre, holds an 11.94 percent stake in the field. Other partners are Den norske stats oljeselskap AS with 41.40 percent, Esso Norge as with 10.33 percent, Deminex Norge AS with 10.03 percent, Idemitsu Petroleum Norge as with 9.60 percent, Norsk Hydro Produksjon ASA with 8.27 percent, Elf Petroleum Norge AS with 5.51 percent, Amerada Hess Norge as with 1.46 percent and Enterprise Oil Norwegian AS with 1.46 percent.
